Question: For how many values of \(n\) will an \(n\)-sided regular polygon have interior angles with integral degree measures?
Solution:
Method 1: Count divisors using prime exponents

For an integer \(n\ge3\), the equal interior angles of a regular \(n\)-gon each measure
\[
\frac{180(n-2)}{n}=180-\frac{360}{n}
\]
degrees. This is an integer exactly when \(360/n\) is an integer, so we need to count the positive divisors of \(360\), excluding \(1\) and \(2\).

Factor
\[
360=2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5.
\]
Every positive divisor has exactly one expression \(2^i3^j5^k\), where
\[
0\le i\le3,\qquad 0\le j\le2,\qquad 0\le k\le1.
\]
There are \(4\) choices for \(i\), \(3\) for \(j\), and \(2\) for \(k\), giving \(4\cdot3\cdot2=24\) divisors. Unique prime factorization ensures that all divisors occur and none is counted twice. Removing \(n=1\) and \(n=2\), which do not form polygons, leaves \(\boxed{22}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).

Method 2: List complementary factor pairs

The exterior angles of a regular \(n\)-gon are equal and sum to \(360^\circ\), so each is \(360/n\) degrees. An interior angle and its adjacent exterior angle add to \(180^\circ\). Thus the interior angles have integral degree measures exactly when \(360/n\) is an integer: \(n\) must divide \(360\), with \(n\ge3\).

We can count these divisors by pairing each divisor \(d\) with \(360/d\). Since
\[
18^2<360<19^2,
\]
every pair has exactly one member at most \(18\). Checking the integers from \(1\) through \(18\) gives all the pairs:
\[
\begin{gathered}
(1,360),\ (2,180),\ (3,120),\\
(4,90),\ (5,72),\ (6,60),\\
(8,45),\ (9,40),\ (10,36),\\
(12,30),\ (15,24),\ (18,20).
\end{gathered}
\]
There are \(12\) pairs, each containing two distinct divisors. Every divisor belongs to exactly one pair, so there are \(24\) divisors altogether. Excluding \(1\) and \(2\) leaves \(\boxed{22}\) possible side counts, choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
